session_summary: Session 8, three acts. ACT 1 — five asks from real use: raw $...$ LaTeX in live interviewer replies (md.py only knew \(...\), and REOPENED interviews rendered nothing at all because only raw markdown is stored); deletable past interviews ordered by last interaction, where delete REBUILDS the skill model from surviving evidence because mastery is an accumulated EMA that cannot be subtracted; a visible Weak-spots tab (the evidence had only ever steered loop composition invisibly); completion badges on all 322 topic cards; and context work — record_behavior had ZERO callers so the behavioural profile was dead code, plus topic_recall for cross-session continuity in counts only. Also found a cross-segment answer leak: the dossier dropped only the LIVE rubric, so a mixed loop could preview a later segment's points — and weak-spot drills build loops from exactly the weakest topics, so the two lists overlap by construction. ACT 2 — HOSTING AND SPEED. Measured with agy's own --log-file that 13.8s of a 16.5s turn is session bootstrap before streamGenerateContent is even called; prompt size is irrelevant and the low tier is no faster while doing ZERO reasoning. Warm/pre-spawned agy is impossible (--prompt-interactive needs a TTY; under a pty it renders a TUI). The user supplied an AI Studio key: API gemini-3.6-flash answers in 5.4s vs agy's 16.1s with IDENTICAL grading. Moved the call server-side (app/interview/cloud.py) so no laptop is needed — 5.0s for a real turn with no worker running — with agy as fallback and the key as a Fly secret. Separately, our OWN worst latency: the lease backed off geometrically while idle, and an interview is mostly idle, so an answer waited ~10s just to be NOTICED. Long poll: discovery 10.0s -> 0.10s. ACT 3 — a 66-agent Grok hunt, 24 of them holding REAL interviews through a new interview_cli.py. 389 findings, 10 real after verification; THREE were misgrading the student — correct answers discarded when a phase advanced mid-exchange (reproduced: answers req3 correctly, report says missed), TAUGHT clawing back stored partial credit, and [PARTIAL] frozen at half credit with the interviewer forbidden to finish the thought. Two of those I had introduced that same morning while fixing the circling. Also fixed: interviews ending mid-question with no summary, curiosity counted as being stuck (which the new stall floor turned into force-closing the phase of the most engaged students), help arriving a turn late, SAFETY/RECITATION-truncated replies accepted as complete, and the report spinner that never resolved (handler got the click Event as its session id). MOBILE: the shell claimed more height than the screen had (html,body height:100% is the LAYOUT viewport, which does not shrink for the keyboard) — one wrong height affecting every tab; and a six-item nav with flex-shrink:0 made the header wider than a phone so the whole page panned into black. CANCELLED: a corpus rewrite I had proposed and the user had approved — opening the files showed both my metrics were artefacts (the 'weak ladder' test flagged tier 3 being SHORTER, which usually means more specific; the 'vendor-locked' test flagged PostgreSQL/Redis points that ARE the subject matter). Re-measured properly: 2 of 1436, both a deliberate convention. 322 rubrics correctly left alone. Invariants 17 -> 105, plus 12 new worker-routing checks.

gotchas: agy: the prompt is ARGV not stdin, and '--print --model X <prompt>' SILENTLY LOSES the prompt; use '--model X --print <prompt>'.
agy tool attempts return NO output at all in headless mode, so looks_valid() + retry is load-bearing.
Do not run two extract/mutation batches plus a server on the same box unattended; /mnt/c (9p) is slow — cache anything that scans the corpus.
_already_running + deleting a test DB is a footgun: the replacement server exits and the old process keeps serving a deleted inode with zero tables. Kill servers before rm-ing their DB.
The grounding audit under-scores formula-heavy topics (mental math 40%) because it counts shared words; gate_rubric.py is the stronger check there.
